column4: A read-only, dependency-free Python CLI skill for querying wallet balances, tokens, transactions, gas, ENS, and security data across eight EVM-compatible chains with USD pricing.
column5: Python 3.8+ stdlib, public RPC endpoints (overridable), free public pricing/ENS/decoding APIs
column12: terminal toolset, script path under the skill's install directory
column14: OPTIONAL - handy read-only blockchain data tool, but niche/vertical-specific
column15: Use whenever a user asks for EVM wallet portfolios, token/contract info, gas prices, ENS lookups, whale transfers, or approval/security checks across 8 chains (Ethereum, BSC, Base, Arbitrum, Polygon, Optimism, Avalanche, zkSync); Run the bundled stdlib-only Python script with a subcommand (wallet, multichain, compare, tx, decode, ens, allowance, contract, whale, gas) rather than calling any external SDK; No credentials are required; pricing/ENS/decoding rely on free public APIs that are rate-limited and have no fallback if down; Watch for known limits: known-token list only covers ~30 tokens per chain, L2 gas estimates omit L1 data-posting fees, and address casing is not checksum-validated; Verify functionality by running the network stats command and an ENS resolution smoke test; Recommend a private RPC endpoint for heavier or production use to avoid public rate limiting

column12: terminal toolset, home-directory .env convention, script path under the skill's install directory
column14: OPTIONAL - vertical-specific trading data tool for Hyperliquid users
column15: Use when a user wants Hyperliquid market data (markets, candles, funding, order book) or to review their own perp/spot account activity and trade quality; Twelve subcommands cover discovery, historical data pulls, live book depth, account state/balances, fills/orders, a heuristic trade review, and a normalized data export for backtesting prep; Configure default network and wallet address via environment variables so most commands can run without repeating the address; Be aware fills/orders endpoints only expose a recent rolling window, not full archive history, and the review command is heuristic, not a precise reconstruction of trader intent; For deep analysis, chain commands: start with review to find problem periods, then pull fills/orders/candles/funding for that window; Verify by running the markets command and confirming top markets by volume print correctly

column4: A stdlib-only Python CLI skill for querying Solana wallet portfolios, SPL token/NFT holdings, transactions, whale transfers, and network stats with USD pricing.
column5: Python stdlib, Solana public RPC endpoint (overridable), free public pricing API
column12: terminal toolset, script path under the skill's install directory
column14: OPTIONAL - vertical-specific blockchain data tool, parallel to the EVM skill
column15: Use for Solana wallet/token/NFT portfolio lookups, transaction inspection, recent activity, whale detection, or SOL/SPL token price checks; Eight subcommands run against a public RPC endpoint with optional price enrichment; no API keys needed; NFT detection is a heuristic (amount=1, decimals=0) so compressed NFTs and newer token-standard NFTs will be missed; Whale detection only scans the most recent block (a point-in-time snapshot) and public RPC transaction history is limited to about two days; Use a private RPC endpoint for production-grade or high-volume use to avoid public rate limits; Verify by running the network stats command and confirming current slot, TPS, and SOL price are returned
